newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela marks 79th birthday with private party.
newsitem.headline: Mandela marks 79th birthday with private party.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela closed the gates on his public life on Friday for a two-day 79th birthday party with his family, including 18 grandchildren, officials said.
Mandela returned with his companion, Graca Machel, from a 10-day visit to Britain, Indonesia and Thailand in the early hours of Friday.
"He is spending today and tomorrow very privately with his family in Pretoria. They will have a party this afternoon and I think maybe it will go on tomorrow," said spokesman Parks Mankahlana.
The celebration was arranged at Mandela's official residence behind heavy gates on a hill overlooking Pretoria.
Officials said they did not know whether Machel, widow of former Mozambican president Samora Machel and Mandela's regular companion for more than a year, would join the party.
Mandela's public birthday celebration was a party in Cape Town three weeks ago for more than 900 children from across the country, all of them suffering life-threatening diseases.

Mankahlana reaffirmed that Mandela would relinquish the leadership of his ruling African National Congress at a conference in December, but he dismissed speculation that Mandela would retire ahead of the next election in 1999.
Mandela has said he would serve only one term as president.
"He will be head of state until 1999 and then he will retire. This speculation about him retiring early is completely unfounded," he said.
Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who controls the day-to-day running of the government, is currently the only candidate for the ANC's leadership election in December.
As party leader, he would be almost certain to succeed Mandela as president in 1999.
Mandela was born into the Xhosa royal family in remote Transkei in 1918.
He and fellow ANC leader Oliver Tambo opened the country's first black legal partnership in Johannesburg before he was arrested in 1962 for fighting white rule and jailed for life.
He was freed in 1990 to begin negotiations that led to his party's runaway victory in South Africa's first all-race elections in May, 1994.
Mandela has built a modern home near his birthplace of Qunu, where he has said he intends to retire.
